$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{y^2}}\,\mathrm{d}y & =\int 2 x + 14\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =\left(x + 7\right)^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution in implicit form is

$$
\sqrt[3]{y}=\left(x + 7\right)^{2}+C.
$$

We're required to write the solution in the form $y=y(x).$ Solving for $y$ gives

$$
y=\left(C + \left(x + 7\right)^{2}\right)^{3}.
$$
